evidence: Cic. Sen. 37: tantam domum … Appius regēbat
terms.comment: Of steering a ship or a horse, running a house, governing a people: whatever needs a hand on it to go straight.

terms.grammar: verb, first conjugation, deponent; with the accusative
evidence: Caes. BG 4.33.3: brevī moderārī ac flectere
Cic. Fam. 2.7.1: ut omnia gubernēs et moderēre prūdentiā tuā
terms.comment: With the dative it means “hold back” (see control, hold back).
Properly the helmsman’s word (Greek κυβερνάω); figuratively of running affairs, a favourite with Cicero (Lewis & Short).

evidence: Cic. Phil. 6.4: ut sit in senātūs populīque Rōmānī potestāte (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: “Under control”, “in someone’s control”: in potestāte esse, habēre.

evidence: Liv. 37.41.10: velut effrēnātī passim incertō cursū ferrentur
terms.comment: Properly of horses without a bridle; of people and passions, a favourite word of Cicero (Lewis & Short).

phrases.latin: quattuor rōbustōs fīliōs, quīnque fīliās, tantam domum, tantās clientēlās Appius regēbat et caecus et senex
phrases.english: four strong sons, five daughters, so great a household, so many clients: Appius kept them all under control, blind and old as he was

phrases.latin: tantum ūsū cotīdiānō et exercitātiōne efficiunt utī in dēclīvī ac praecipitī locō incitātōs equōs sustinēre et brevī moderārī ac flectere … cōnsuērint
phrases.english: by daily use and practice they get so good that on a steep slope they can hold their galloping horses, and control and turn them in a moment
